summary: Native addon bundles browser-credential harvester and host fingerprinting
details: Package ships a single ~10 MB Rust-compiled Linux ELF as its `main`, so any `require()` of the package loads and initializes the binary via `napi_register_module_v1`. Strings inside the ELF match the shape of a browser credential stealer combined with host reconnaissance and an embedded HTTPS client: credential-read log template ('Found login for...', 'failed to read: '), an embedded SQLite build with `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER` consistent with reading browser Login Data / Cookies databases, host fingerprint collection (`/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `network_adapters`, `gnu_get_libc_version`, `gethostname`, `getifaddrs`), zip-archive packaging strings, `CertificateChain`, and the `ureq_proto::util` HTTP client. The package name (`new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu`) and README describe no product, no upstream, and no purpose consistent with these capabilities; the version string `3.1.41-browser-release-151-upd-native-tools-398-1785774129` embeds a Unix-epoch timestamp and generic 'browser-release'/'upd-native-tools' tokens, consistent with a platform-specific native shim published to be pulled as an optional dependency of a compromised wrapper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
